posts.author: Susanpossibly
posts.body:
Doubt anyone will read this other than me, but in the off chance I'm wrong:
Hello! I've been a long time fan of the RPG Maker engine since RPG Maker 2003, and I decided that I'm (finally) going to try my hand at releasing more serious projects. Originally, this idea came to me as a way to "Do a small project to start off." Unfortunately, like many others, small mindless projects often end up more developed than intended. Oops, that's my bad.
Personal feelings aside, let me tell you about this silly little project.
__________________________________________________________________________________________________________
​
[SYNOPSIS]
You, the player, wake up in a mysterious, humble library with no recollection of who or where you are. Upon leaving, you meet your first acquaintance: The Painter. She is initially surprised to see you awake and immediately begins referring to you as "The Writer".
You and The Painter sit together in a back room of the library as she explains that you have 100 days to befriend the townsfolk and improve the town before the Festival of Enlightenment.
Collect resources, create bonds, and bring beauty into the humble town of Vellichor. Will you focus on your social relationships, or will you focus on developing your artistic abilities to make the town feel whole?
Explore the peaceful town of Vellichor, and exhale sharply out of your nose at the collection of silly jokes, hand drawn assets, and peculiar tone that this multi-ending game/visual novel has to offer.
(The Library: The first room you'll see in the game opening.)
(Dramatic cut-in to show that fishing is serious business.)
(The overdramatic weeding sequence)
Lil Features so far:
Audible footsteps
A functional time system where you spend mornings, afternoons, and evenings outside, and nights at home.
Hand drawn colored pencil portraits, made by me, obviously, because they're not that good, BUT THEY ARE CHARMING AND YOU ARE CHARMED.
Custom background music.
Every game's mandatory fishing "minigame"
A lot of unserious nonsense.
__________________________________________________________________________________________________________
Sorry if this is a little early in development to be talking about this project, I just wanted to share some of the work I've been doing the last couple months. I'm not an egomaniac, so any feedback/constructive criticism is welcome! Thank you
​

posts.author: Susanpossibly
posts.body:
Okay, so I’ve begun drawing the cut-ins for the different events, and I just finished putting them in, and just as expected, they look exceptionally dumb. Which is my goal.
Still trying to figure out what to draw for the large fish, and if there should be a cut-in for catching nothing.
As far as game-feel goes, I’m enjoying it. The whole thing still looks kind of clunky, but for a first project, I’m not that mad.
As far as the scope of my reach, I hope this continues to grow. I still need to draft up official art for several other main characters, as well as do the sprite work, but it’s materializing.

posts.author: Susanpossibly
posts.body:
A few weeks of silence but I HAVE been working on this. Here is where I'm at.
-Added more hand drawn assets to differentiate the art style.
Spoiler:
CustomAssets
-Updated sprites and have been continuing work on portraits.
Spoiler:
Sprites
-Partially set up Library bookshelves to display heart levels with different characters
Spoiler:
Hearts
-Set the menu up so it's closer to what it's supposed to look like (And doesn't have an HP bar)
Spoiler:
Menu
-I've also been writing the different character heart events
-Brainstorming Minigames
I've been taking my time, but I don't think I've been slacking. A lot of my time has been spent focusing on getting all the assets finished, so I've been away from the program itself for a second. I'm only slightly worried I'll forget how to do everything.
Endings aren't fully realized yet, and tbh, I'm worried about the sheer number of different branched endings I'm going to have (Ideally, around 100, realistically, maybe 20.) I'm also trying to give each character's heart event a life lesson for YOU THE PLAYER!
Not to sound sappy, but I'm putting my whole soul into this. Over the last few years, I've had to give up some life goals and dreams because of chronic health issues, so this has been a delightful escape. RPG Maker gets an unfair reputation, and I hope to make something that gets people to reconsider it's potential and maybe even inspire someone else to create something.
I'll update again in the future. Hopefully, next update the character assets will all be finished and I can strictly focus on the writing/programming aspects.
If you read this far, hi! Hope you're having a good day.

posts.author: Susanpossibly
posts.body:
Another update!
The main character base sprites are all finished. With that done, I feel like I can finally start working on the actual technical parts of the game.
I've got a prototype set up for 2 of my minigames.
-One is a simple pattern tracing minigame where you have a short time frame to cut out a panel for a piece of fabric. The visuals are still a work in progress, I just wanted to make sure I could get it working first.
-The other one I have set up is a simple "Avoid the moving obstacles" minigame. Gonna make a few variations of both maps to keep things interesting. I was playtesting that one for a while, and it's turning out pretty fun.
I have a piano prototype for another mini game, but no playable element other than making the keys make noise. Currently spending time character building before I write any concrete dialogue.
Still gotta draw up a couple more building interiors, but things are still coming together. I'm starting to get to the point where I'll publicly advertising its development. Aiming to have enough done to officially announce it around Christmas.
Step by step it's coming together. Just keep swimming.
